description: As head of the defence department, Pfister presented the Federal Council's 2026 army despatch, which proposed an overall increase of around 3.4 billion francs and prioritised ground-based air defence, drone defence and cyber security. It included an additional credit (reported at roughly 394-400 million francs) for the F-35 fighter jet programme to cover cost increases since the popular vote, and indicated the planned fleet would be reduced from 36 to around 30 jets.
significance: Central defence-financing package of Pfister's tenure, shaping Swiss rearmament priorities and the contested F-35 procurement.

law_name: Proposed temporary VAT increase to finance the army
description: Pfister advanced a plan to finance higher army spending partly through a temporary increase of value-added tax (reported at around 0.8 percentage points from 2028 for about ten years), consistent with his stated preference for raising revenue rather than loosening the federal debt brake.
significance: Signals his approach to defence financing through additional revenue rather than debt, a notable policy stance for the defence minister.
